narrative.headline: 2019 Ford Edge: transmission and engine top owner complaints
narrative.summary: Owners filed 712 complaints with NHTSA. Most point to the power train (418 reports, 59%) and the engine (148 reports, 21%) - together roughly 4 out of 5 complaints. These are the areas to test hard before you buy and watch closely if you own one. A handful of reports describe a crash, and one notes an injury; none mention a fire.

issues.title: Power Train
issues.blurb: By far the biggest concern: 418 reports (59% of all complaints). Owners describe the car hesitating to shift or not accelerating when they hit the gas. Linked to 4 crashes and 1 injury - take a test drive with hard acceleration and watch for delayed or rough shifting.

issues.title: Engine
issues.blurb: The second most common area: 148 reports (21%). Reports include the engine shutting down or losing power while driving. Tied to 1 crash - listen for stalling or warning lights during a longer test drive.

issues.title: Electrical System
issues.blurb: A smaller but notable group: 34 reports (5%), with 2 crashes. Owners describe electrical faults that can leave the car without power - check that lights, hazards, and dashboard warnings all work.

issues.blurb: 33 reports (5%), no crashes or injuries. Reports describe rough running and sudden loss of power while driving - another reason to drive the car long enough to feel how the engine behaves at speed.
